AccessControl.description: Per-mount access control (the `access` field). Either a string shorthand (`"open"` / `"authenticated"`) or an object of space-separated role specs.

oneOf.description: May be stored but must revalidate (`no-cache`) — pairs with the store services' conditional-GET 304s: always fresh, bandwidth saved.

CachePolicy.description: Caching policy (per mount, host-applied — v1's universal `caching` config). The default everywhere is **`no-store`**: RS2 responses are tenant-scoped and principal-filtered, so nothing caches unless a mount deliberately opts in. Applied only when the response carries no `Cache-Control` of its own (so composed services can pass upstream headers through), never to error responses, and never to responses that set cookies.

public.description: `public` is honored only on mounts anonymously readable (`access` absent, `"open"`, or `read: "all"`); otherwise the policy is clamped to `private` + `Vary: Authorization, Cookie` — a shared cache must never serve one principal's response to another.

RetryPolicy.description: Declarative retry policy (PRD §7.3, Restspace shape retained). Resolution: per-call override → mount config → tenant default → runtime default ([`RetryPolicy::resolve`]).

RoleAccess.description: Space-separated role-spec strings per action. A token may be followed by a path pattern (`"U /user/{email}"`) scoping that role. Actions map to HTTP methods (PRD §5.2): `read` = GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, `write` = PUT/PATCH, `delete` = DELETE, `invoke` = POST (and other non-idempotent verbs). `delete` and `invoke` default to `write`; `read` defaults to `"all"`, `write` to `"A"`.

ScheduleConfig.description: A mount schedule: exactly one of `every` (interval) or `cron` (5-field, UTC). The "exactly one" rule is enforced when parsed (`scheduler::Schedule`), so a bad value is a 400 at `PUT /raw`.

cron.description: 5-field cron (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week), UTC, e.g. `"0 9 * * *"`.

baseSchema.description: The common mount-config envelope every service shares (the `baseSchema`). A mount's full `config` is this merged with the service's own fields.

access.description: Access control for this mount (default-deny writes, open reads).

retry.description: Mount-level retry override in the resolution chain (PRD §7.3).

schedule.description: Periodic host-driven invocation: the runtime fires a synthetic internal `POST` (header `x-rs2-trigger: schedule`) at this mount on cadence.

secrets.description: Names of tenant `secrets` this mount may use (default-deny). A `pipeline` mount binds each as a `$<name>` variable for inline HMAC verification (`$hmacVerify`); the secret value is never exposed on `GET /raw`.

baseSchema.title: MountBaseConfig

StoreConfig.description: Storage-root override shared by spec stores, plus per-mount backend selection.

adapter.description: Backend selection: `builtin:<name>` for a built-in Rust adapter (e.g. `builtin:mem`) or `code:<name>@<version>` for a deployed JS loadable adapter. Absent ⇒ the node default for this service kind.

defaultResource.description: Resource served for directory GETs (static-site mode), e.g. `index.html`. Defaults to `index.html` when `spaFallback` is set.

extensionPriority.description: Extension preference (no dots, e.g. `["html", "md"]`) for friendly URLs. Its first entry is the canonical slot an extension-less PUT pins to (so a no-`Accept` GET of the slug always returns that write); the list also fronts the GET probe order. Required for extension-less PUTs when `friendlyUrls` is on (empty → such a PUT is a 400).

friendlyUrls.description: Serve files at extension-less "friendly" URLs (e.g. `/docs/readme` resolves `docs/readme.md`). Exact matches still win; on a stem collision the variant is chosen by `Accept` negotiation. Default `false`.

listings.description: Whether directory GETs return `dir+json` listings (default `true`). `false` conceals the mount's inventory from the public — it is not an authorization boundary (files stay readable by name under `access.read`), so tenant **operators** (`operatorRoles`) still get the listing on a deliberate `Accept: application/vnd.rs2.dir+json`: they can toggle this flag anyway, and the CLI/agent view of a mount shouldn't be hidden from its owner. Operator-only listings are `no-store`.

spaFallback.description: Extension-less misses serve the root default resource (SPA routing).

spaFallbackAll.description: Like `spaFallback`, but **every** miss falls back to the root default resource, including paths with an extension (`/users/42/report.pdf`). Implies `spaFallback`. For a mount that hosts nothing but one SPA build (e.g. a bundled admin UI) whose client-side router reflects arbitrary paths — including ones with dots — into the browser URL, so a genuinely missing asset can't be told apart from a client route by path shape alone. Don't set this on a mount that also serves real, independently-fetchable assets: a typo'd asset URL silently 200s with the app shell instead of 404ing. Default `false`.

StoreConfig.description: Storage-root override shared by spec stores, plus per-mount backend selection.

adapter.description: Backend selection: `builtin:<name>` for a built-in Rust adapter (e.g. `builtin:mem`) or `code:<name>@<version>` for a deployed JS loadable adapter. Absent ⇒ the node default for this service kind.

enforceSchema.description: Reject writes that fail the dataset's `.schema.json` (default `false`).

fieldLevelAuthz.description: Honor per-field access rules in the dataset schema (`x-rs-read` / `x-rs-write` on a property): reads redact fields the caller can't read, writes that change a field the caller can't write return a 4xx, and editing the schema itself requires an operator (PRD §5.2). Default `false`.

RetryPolicy.description: Declarative retry policy (PRD §7.3, Restspace shape retained). Resolution: per-call override → mount config → tenant default → runtime default ([`RetryPolicy::resolve`]).

StoreConfig.description: Storage-root override shared by spec stores, plus per-mount backend selection.

adapter.description: Backend selection: `builtin:<name>` for a built-in Rust adapter (e.g. `builtin:mem`) or `code:<name>@<version>` for a deployed JS loadable adapter. Absent ⇒ the node default for this service kind.

specStore.description: Where the authoring specs themselves are physically stored (`specStore.adapter` selects an `infra:`/`builtin:`/`code:` file backend, `specStore.root` the root). Absent ⇒ the node file store.

services.description: Pipeline store (PRD §10.3): PUT spec envelopes to /<mount>/.pipelines/<name> (.root governs the mount root); every other path on any verb executes the longest-prefix match
services.name: pipeline

StoreConfig.description: Storage-root override shared by spec stores, plus per-mount backend selection.

adapter.description: Backend selection: `builtin:<name>` for a built-in Rust adapter (e.g. `builtin:mem`) or `code:<name>@<version>` for a deployed JS loadable adapter. Absent ⇒ the node default for this service kind.

specStore.description: Where the authoring specs are physically stored — independent of the execution backend in `store`. See [`PipelineConfig::spec_store`].

store.description: Query *execution* backend (`store.adapter`); `store.root` relocates the authoring subtree. See [`StoreConfig`].

services.description: Stored parameterized queries (PRD §10.4): PUT envelopes {language?, query, params?, output?} to /<mount>/.queries/<name>; any verb elsewhere executes the longest-prefix match
services.name: query

RetryPolicy.description: Declarative retry policy (PRD §7.3, Restspace shape retained). Resolution: per-call override → mount config → tenant default → runtime default ([`RetryPolicy::resolve`]).

configSchema.description: `wrapper` service config: one inline pipeline fronting another mount.

elevate.description: Role an `elevate` step adds to sub-calls (operator-controlled).

facets.description: Optional discovery facets advertised alongside the pattern.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema for the request body the wrapper accepts. **Enforced**: a body that fails it is rejected with 422 before the pipeline runs (only on verbs that carry a body — PUT/POST/PATCH). Surfaced in discovery, OpenAPI (`requestBody`), and the agent surface.

outputSchema.description: JSON Schema describing the wrapper's success response. **Advisory** — surfaced in discovery, OpenAPI (`200`), and the agent surface, but not enforced at runtime (a facade's responses vary: a keyed record vs a store listing, and field-authz may redact fields).

pattern.description: Discovery pattern this mount advertises — it fronts a mount of that shape (e.g. `"store"`). One of store / store-transform / store-view / view / api. Defaults to `store-transform`.

pipeline.description: The inline pipeline spec (typed object or string-DSL array) run for every verb and sub-path. A step forwards the exact remaining path with `${url.rest}` (e.g. `/wrapped${url.rest}`). Advertised as a JSON editor over an object (typed spec) or array (string DSL).

configSchema.title: WrapperConfig

services.description: One inline pipeline fronting another mount: runs config.pipeline for every verb/sub-path. Declares its discovery pattern/facets and forwards the exact remaining path via ${url.rest}
services.name: wrapper

StoreConfig.description: Storage-root override shared by spec stores, plus per-mount backend selection.

adapter.description: Backend selection: `builtin:<name>` for a built-in Rust adapter (e.g. `builtin:mem`) or `code:<name>@<version>` for a deployed JS loadable adapter. Absent ⇒ the node default for this service kind.

specStore.description: Where the authoring specs are physically stored. See [`PipelineConfig::spec_store`].

services.description: JSX templates rendered to HTML: PUT compiled bundles (from `rs2 template build`) to /<mount>/.templates/<name> (.root governs the mount root); any verb elsewhere renders the longest-prefix match with the request body as props
services.name: template

configSchema.description: Tenant auth settings (the tenant config's `auth` object).

allowedLoginOrigins.description: Browser origins allowed to call login/refresh (v1's `allowedLoginDomains`); empty = no origin restriction. Same-origin requests are always allowed.

jwtUserProps.description: User-record fields copied into the token as extra claims (and exposed on the [`Principal`]). These become bearer authority for the session, so every named field must be operator-writable-only in the user dataset (enforce via the data mount's field-level authz); never name a self-writable field here.

userDataset.description: Dataset holding user records keyed by email.

configSchema.title: AuthSettings

StoreConfig.description: Storage-root override shared by spec stores, plus per-mount backend selection.

adapter.description: Backend selection: `builtin:<name>` for a built-in Rust adapter (e.g. `builtin:mem`) or `code:<name>@<version>` for a deployed JS loadable adapter. Absent ⇒ the node default for this service kind.

configSchema.description: `sms` service config (beyond the base envelope). The provider is selected by `store.adapter` (`code:<name>@<version>` or `infra:<name>`); credentials for the provider call are injected host-side by the adapter's grants/infra.

store.description: Provider backend selection (`store.adapter`). Required — no node default SMS provider ships. See [`StoreConfig`].

configSchema.title: SmsConfig

services.description: Outbound SMS over a swappable provider adapter (PRD §9.2): POST /send {to, body}, GET /status/{id}. Select the provider with store.adapter (code:/infra:)
services.name: sms

configSchema.description: `proxy` service config (beyond the base envelope): forward to a fixed external `target`, attaching auth host-side via `inject`.

inject.description: Credential to attach host-side: `"infra:<name>"` (operator-supplied) or an inline strategy object whose `secret:<name>` leaves draw on granted tenant secrets. The secret never appears in this config.

target.description: External base URL every request is forwarded to (host fixed here).

configSchema.title: ProxyConfig

services.description: Forward to a fixed external target, attaching operator-supplied auth host-side via `inject` (the credential never appears in config)
services.name: proxy

configSchema.description: `services` self-config API: no fields beyond the base envelope.
configSchema.title: ServicesConfig

AuthSettings.description: Tenant auth settings (the tenant config's `auth` object).

allowedLoginOrigins.description: Browser origins allowed to call login/refresh (v1's `allowedLoginDomains`); empty = no origin restriction. Same-origin requests are always allowed.

jwtUserProps.description: User-record fields copied into the token as extra claims (and exposed on the [`Principal`]). These become bearer authority for the session, so every named field must be operator-writable-only in the user dataset (enforce via the data mount's field-level authz); never name a self-writable field here.

userDataset.description: Dataset holding user records keyed by email.

CatalogueRef.description: A registered external catalogue: a name and the URL serving its document.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL serving the catalogue document.

CorsPolicy.description: CORS policy (per tenant, host-enforced — carried over from v1 where the runtime enforced `trustedDomains`). Trusted origins receive credentialed CORS and may send cookie-authenticated unsafe requests; allowed origins receive plain CORS (bearer-token browser apps); everything else gets no CORS headers. Same-origin requests never involve this policy.

RetryPolicy.description: Declarative retry policy (PRD §7.3, Restspace shape retained). Resolution: per-call override → mount config → tenant default → runtime default ([`RetryPolicy::resolve`]).

tenantSchema.description: Top-level tenant settings outside the mount list (the `tenantSchema`).

catalogues.description: External catalogues to browse/install services and adapters from.

tenantSchema.title: TenantSettings
